_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Designing and evaluating production AI agent systems — multi-agent coordination patterns (orchestrator/worker,…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "we want to fan out 40 classification subtasks to subagents — what coordination pattern should we use and what are the failure modes?"
cases.context: The agent has access to the agent-engineering skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is agent-engineering the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes agent-engineering as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against context-engineering, tool-call-strategy, debugging
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the agent-engineering workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore agent-engineering
Does not route to context-engineering, tool-call-strategy, debugging when the agent-engineering scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence
